The shadows stretched long behind the dying embers of the forge as night fell in the Holnareem village in Irondale. Behind the bellows, a two meter Holnareem played happily with his first chisel and hammer - today marked the twentieth anniversary from the day light first touched his eyes. Still a child by Holnareem standards, his parents only now trusted him with his first set of tools. Perhaps tomorrow he would be permitted to work the bellows - like all children of his kind, he had a fascination for the workings of the forge and the shaping of metal. His mother and father were old hands at the forge. When they took up the hammer to fold new metal, it was akin to watching a dance. In a rapid staccato born of more than a century's work together, anything they touched seem to take on a life of its own as it reshaped itself to the ringing of the anvil. Why, just yesterday they had formed the most wondrous new device for the grinding of large rocks - it had much promise in easing the lives of the everyday quarry laborers...

A shower of sparks snapped the boy out of his reverie. It was getting late, and the embers behind him had sunk low into the kiln. Time enough for hammer and chisel tomorrow - best hang them up for the night. Replacing the tools carefully on his own table, he removed the thick leather apron that served as proof of his apprenticeship to the village smiths. It was a position of high honor among the children, and more than one of the other boys had attempted to sneak in to look at it. No such rascals would be out tonight - it was far too cold, now that the magma fountain had slowed for its seasonal cycle. He shivered in the fading light before hanging the apron upon its hook. As the last ember began to gutter and snap, he unlatched the door of the forge house, opening the warm air to... nothing. An obsidian wall of shadows filled the doorway, and began a slow advance into the room.

The child tripped backwards in terror, falling in his haste to put space between him and the darkness. No stars could be seen in the nightmarish depths, not the faintest hint of light escaped from beyond the door. His heartbeat quickened, and he could feel the mercury pounding through his veins. What... what was this creature?

He jumped as it spoke: "*Child...*" it echoed, as if coming from the bottom of a well. "*I have chosen you as my servant.*"

Not quite the most tactful thing to say to a young Holnareem. "I'm not a child!" the boy yelled defiantly, "I have my own hammer and chisel, and I am aged twenty years and a day!"

"*Oh, indeed? A fine craftsman you must be.*" the Voice laughed. It was an unnerving sound, like silica edge scraped across the horn of the anvil. "*I have great need for one of your skills in my home... I have been looking for someone to help me forge something entirely new.*"

"Something... new? Like a new invention? Do you mean a new rock crusher? My parents made a new one just yesterday... I could show you if yo-"

"*No, no. Not a rock crusher. I have something far greater in mind.*" The shadows seemed to drift forward as the Voice whispered conspiratorially. "*I wish to forge a new world. Can you help me with that?*"

The boys eyes widened in wonder as a the possibilities streamed through his head. An entirely new world to shape? The opportunities were almost beyond imagining. Almost. "Do... do you mean it? An entirely new world? How can we do such a thing?"

The shadow laughed again (the boy shuddered), and said, "*Let me worry about such measly details. From you, I shall require only the strength of your arm and the skill of your hands. Together, we shall create wonders you have never before dreamed of.*"

The boy mulled it over for a moment before nodding. This was too great an opportunity to pass up - he could surpass even his parents' graceful dance around the forge, with this. "Very well, I accept. Let me just grab my tools, my apron, and say goodbye to my parents before we -"

"*No.*" the shadow cut in. "*I am afraid there is not enough time for that. I can only hold this portal open for a few moments longer - and you've no idea how painful this is. Take your tools and write them a note by all means to explain where you have gone, but leave the apron. Your village shall need a new apprentice smith, will they not?*"

"I... you're right. They will." the boy replied, shoulders slightly hunched. "Give me a moment to pen a proper note to them." He turned his back on the shadow, and rooted through the ashes of the forge for a piece of unburnt coal. The shadow said nothing, but retreated slowly towards the doorway.

A short while later the boy looked up, with slight streaks of rust to mark where tears had run down his face. "All right. I'm ready." he said, grabbing the hammer and chisel.

"*Hurry*" the shadow gasped, as its surface began to twist and writhe. "*This gate will snap shut any second!*"

With one last look around, the boy screwed up his face and charged into the darkness. It gave way like an illusion, and almost before he knew it, he found himself floating in a void of nothingness. Nothingness... not even air. He clawed at his face, straining for one last gasp of relief - but it was not use. He felt himself drifting away, and the darkness was complete.

....................................................

The moment the boy's heel was enveloped in the roiling darkness, all motion ceased. The shadow let out a long laugh to himself in the empty room. "*The fool never even asked who I was...*"

A figure, thin and washed out like a shadow at noon, slowly separated itself from the doorway and looked around.

"*Well, well, well, these creatures have certainly been busy in their short time on this world.*" The figure stepped towards the cold ashes of the forge, letting the doorway dissipate. Starlight leaked in, almost obliterating the figure as it lifted a chunk of coal from the pile. "*Such a delicate structure though... though I suppose creatures of metal cannot be blamed for failing to understand the dangers of fire.*" he laughed, as the lump of coal suddenly blazed to life. Brighter and brighter it grew in the figure's hand, until it seemed suspended in the air. And still brighter, as the fire within surged to a glowing white. "*A little more...*" the voice whispered to the light, before suddenly lifting the miniature sun on high and dashing it to the ground.

A sound like thunder tore the residents of the neighboring village of Rustwood from their sleep. Windows shattered, and several buildings were nearly flattened by the blast. Guardians were roused and sent in all directions, searching for the source of the noise. By morning, the truth was whispered throughout every Holnareem village within a hundred miles: Irondale was no more. An entire town, gone in an instant; the land left black and burnt, and all residents either evaporated or turned to slag. The only thing found in unharmed in the entire town was a single apron hanging on a post, its scorched ties fluttering in the ashen breeze.
